newsitem.title: Singapore: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit underpinned by trade data.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit underpinned by trade data.

text.p: * Malaysian ringgit firms after failing to breach key technical level overnight. News of trade surplus provides support.
* Indonesian rupiah gains amid tightened liquidity and calm start to election campaign.
* Singapore dollar rises on large U.S. dollar sale by U.S. fund, but market still within recent range.
* Thai baht slips on low short-term interest rates.
The Malaysian ringgit firmed on Tuesday after failing to weaken beyond a key technical level against the dollar overnight.
Dealers said the ringgit was also supported by news of a trade surplus for February, but the market showed little immediate reaction to a figure within market expectations.
The Statistics Department said Malaysia posted a 367.2 million ringgit trade surplus in February against a revised deficit of 102.9 million for January.

"The downside is limited for dollar/ringgit because the Malaysian stock market is still very weak. Fund managers are downsizing their weightage on Malaysia and that's creating an outflow," a European bank dealer in Singapore said.
He said the ringgit was unlikely to strengthen beyond 2.5025 to the dollar while its downside looked cushioned at 2.5150 after the dollar's repeated failure to breach that level.

"If 2.5150 breaks, there'd be a lot of stop-loss buying and it could go for 2.5300. But I don't think the Malaysian authorities would like that given that funds are needed for financing mega-projects," he said.
The ringgit stood at 2.5087/97 to the dollar at 0435 GMT.
The Singapore dollar firmed on the back of a large U.S. dollar sell order around the 1.4460 level.
"One U.S. name sold a huge amount, probably in the region of $150-200 (million). There was no particular reason. Maybe it's just some commercial interest," the European bank dealer said.
He said there was also local corporate interest in selling the U.S. dollar above S$1.4470, but it was likely to stay supported at S$1.4420.
In Indonesia, the rupiah was firmer amid tightened money market liquidity and a calm start to the campaign for the May 29 general election.
Jakarta dealers said liquidity concerns were the main focus, helping the rupiah regain further ground after rising 10 points on Monday.
"It's mainly liquidity-driven. But the relatively peaceful election campaign seems to calm the market," a local bank dealer said.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,425.00/26.00 at 0435 GMT after reaching a high of 2,422.75 from an opening of 2,426.25/27.25.
The rupiah fell sharply against the dollar to a historic low of 2,440.5 last weak on fears of possible violence during the campaign period lasting till May 23.
A foreign bank dealer said the rupiah was currently capped at the 2,424.0 level on customer orders.
A Singapore-based dealer said 2,420.0 represented an important technical support level for the dollar.
"Medium-term players are still going long on dollars but after the election, there'll probably be a large sell-off," he said.
The Thai baht gave way to continued demand for the dollar in the face of low short-term interest rates, dealers said.
The baht was quoted at 26.121/26.131 to the dollar at 0435 GMT against 26.110/26.145 late on Monday. The central bank fixed the mid-rate at 26.11 per dollar, unchanged from Monday.
"There was continued dollar buying from yesterday as the short-term (baht) interest rates are very low," a local bank dealer in Bangkok said.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703090)
